lessons.title: Krimi oder Komödie? Film types
lessons.goal: Name film types with their articles and plurals, describe them after sein, and say which you prefer and why with gern, lieber, am liebsten, als, weil and dass.

grammar.point: Film types are nouns with an article; in a compound noun the last part gives the article (der Liebesfilm). After sein an adjective has no ending: Krimis sind spannend. Use gern, lieber and am liebsten with film types; lieber is followed by als, not wie. Compare with -er + als and nicht so ... wie. Give reasons with weil and opinions with dass; the verb goes to the end. For general talk use the plural without article: Ich mag Krimis.
grammar.oneLine: Ich sehe lieber Krimis als Liebesfilme, weil ich Krimis spannender finde.

mistake.wrong: Ich sehe lieber Krimis wie Liebesfilme.
mistake.right: Ich sehe lieber Krimis als Liebesfilme.
mistake.why: Lieber is a comparison, and a comparison with -er or lieber always uses als. Wie belongs to so ... wie.

terms.meaning: one long noun made of two or more words, for example Liebes + Film; the last part gives the article
a kind of film or book, for example crime or comedy
for things in general you can use the plural alone: Ich mag Krimis

cards.title: Before we start: what do you like to watch?
cards.body: Everybody has a favourite kind of film: a thriller, a comedy, a cartoon. Talking about films is one of the easiest ways to start a conversation, and one of the best ways to practise your opinions. Today you learn the names of the film types and use your comparisons and dass sentences to say what you like.

examples.de: Ich gucke am liebsten Serien.
examples.en: I like watching series best.
examples.why: You know this already: your favourite way to watch.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass Serien spannender als Filme sind.
examples.en: I think that series are more exciting than films.
examples.why: You know this too: a comparison inside a dass clause.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass Krimis spannender als Komödien sind.
examples.en: I think that crime films are more exciting than comedies.
examples.why: New today: the same pattern with film types.

cards.more: Think of a video shop with shelves. Each shelf has a name: crime, comedy, cartoon, horror. Today you learn the names of the shelves, so that you can say which shelf you like best and why. You do not need new grammar. You use what you know: comparisons with als, gern, lieber and am liebsten, and dass and weil clauses. Only the nouns are new, and they all have an article, so you learn the article together with the word.
steps: You already know: gucken and am liebsten (lesson 3), and Ich finde, dass ... (lesson 4).
New today: the names of film types, with articles and plurals.
By the end you can: say which type of film you prefer and give a reason.

cards.title: Film types and their articles
cards.body: Every film type is a noun, so it has an article. Many types are compound nouns with Film at the end, for example Liebesfilm. In a compound noun the last part gives the article: der Film, so der Liebesfilm. Learn the article together with the word.
cards.lead: You have used der, die and das since the first chapters. Film types are new nouns, so here you meet eight of them and learn how to find the article of a long word.

examples.de: Der Krimi ist spannend.
examples.en: The crime film is exciting.

examples.de: Die Komödie ist witzig.
examples.en: The comedy is funny.

examples.de: Der Dokumentarfilm ist lang.
examples.en: The documentary is long.

deeper.text: A compound noun can be very long, for example Science-Fiction-Film. Do not panic. Look at the last part only: Film is der, so the whole word is der. Zeichentrickfilm ends in film as well, so it is der Zeichentrickfilm. The words Krimi and Komödie are not compounds, so you learn their articles by heart.

example.de: Der Science-Fiction-Film ist spannend.
example.en: The science fiction film is exciting.

cards.more: German likes to glue words together. Liebes + Film makes Liebesfilm, a film about love. The new word is a noun, and its article comes from the last word, the one on the right. That is the big trick: you only need the article of Film (der) to know the article of six film types. Krimi (der) and Komödie (die) stand alone, so just learn them. Always say the article when you learn a noun, for example der Krimi, not only Krimi.

cards.title: Describe a film type: only after sein
cards.body: To say what a type of film is like, use sein and an adjective: Krimis sind spannend. After sein the adjective stays short, with no ending. You already know spannend, witzig, traurig and langweilig. Today gruselig is new: it means scary.
cards.lead: Now that you can name the film types, you want to say what they are like. A short pattern with sein and one adjective is enough.

examples.de: Horrorfilme sind gruselig.
examples.en: Horror films are scary.

examples.de: Komödien sind witzig.
examples.en: Comedies are funny.

examples.de: Dokumentarfilme sind oft langweilig.
examples.en: Documentaries are often boring.

deeper.text: You can make the adjective stronger with sehr or weaker with nicht. Sehr stands before the adjective, nicht too: Der Film ist sehr gruselig. Der Film ist nicht traurig. The adjective itself never changes after sein. This is the easiest place to use adjectives, so use it a lot.

example.de: Der Film ist sehr gruselig.
example.en: The film is very scary.

cards.more: Imagine the adjective as a label that you stick on the noun. After sein the label has no ending: der Film ist spannend, die Komödie ist witzig, die Filme sind traurig. The noun can be singular or plural, the label stays the same. Only the verb changes: ist for one, sind for many. Try it with a film that you know. Which label fits? Spannend, witzig, traurig, langweilig or gruselig?

cards.title: gern, lieber, am liebsten with films
cards.body: You can say how much you like something with three steps: gern (like), lieber (prefer) and am liebsten (like most). For a film type, put the type after the verb: Ich sehe gern Komödien. To compare two types after lieber, use als: lieber Krimis als Liebesfilme.
cards.lead: You learned gern, lieber and am liebsten earlier, and you can compare with als. Here you join both ideas and use them with film types.

examples.de: Ich sehe gern Komödien.
examples.en: I like watching comedies.

examples.de: Ich sehe lieber Krimis als Liebesfilme.
examples.en: I prefer watching crime films to romance films.

examples.de: Ich sehe am liebsten Actionfilme.
examples.en: I like watching action films most.

deeper.text: Which verb do you use for watching: sehen, gucken or schauen? All three work for films. Sehen is neutral. Gucken is informal and very common in the north and in Berlin. Schauen is the usual word in the south, in Bavaria, Austria and Switzerland. Natives choose by region, not by rule, so you can pick one and stay with it. The rest of the sentence with gern, lieber or am liebsten stays exactly the same.

example.de: Ich schaue lieber Krimis.
example.en: I prefer watching crime films.

cards.more: Three steps like a staircase: gern is the first step, lieber is the second, am liebsten is the top. The verb stays the same: Ich sehe. Only the little word changes. When you stand on the second step you look down at the first one, so you name what you like less with als. German says Krimis als Liebesfilme, like English prefer crime films to romance films. And what you do not like, you can say with nicht gern.

rows: Ich sehe lieber Krimis als Liebesfilme.

steps: Choose the verb: Ich sehe
Choose the step: gern / lieber / am liebsten
Say the film type: Komödien
For lieber, add als and the second type: als Liebesfilme

cards.title: Compare film types
cards.body: Compare film types with the comparative and als: Horrorfilme sind gruseliger als Krimis. When two things are not equal, say nicht so ... wie: Komödien sind nicht so spannend wie Actionfilme. Remember: -er goes with als, so goes with wie.
cards.lead: Comparing is something you already do well. Now you compare film types, not people or objects, and you keep als and wie in the right place.

examples.de: Horrorfilme sind gruseliger als Krimis.
examples.en: Horror films are scarier than crime films.

examples.de: Komödien sind nicht so spannend wie Actionfilme.
examples.en: Comedies are not as exciting as action films.

examples.de: Ein Krimi ist so lang wie ein Liebesfilm.
examples.en: A crime film is as long as a romance film.

deeper.text: Gruselig ends in -ig and gets just -er: gruseliger. Spannend becomes spannender, witzig becomes witziger and traurig becomes trauriger. In this lesson the adjective always stands after sein, so it never gets an ending. You can also say genauso witzig wie when two things are equal.

example.de: Der Krimi ist genauso spannend wie der Actionfilm.
example.en: The crime film is just as exciting as the action film.

cards.more: To compare, ask yourself: is one thing more, or are two things equal? If one is more, add -er to the adjective and use als: gruseliger als. If they are equal, use so ... wie: so lang wie. If one is less, say nicht so ... wie. Notice that the second part is just a noun: als Krimis, wie Actionfilme. You do not need a verb there. Short and easy.

rows: Der Film ist so lang wie die Serie.
Komödien sind nicht so spannend wie Actionfilme.

cards.title: Reasons and opinions: weil and dass
cards.body: Give a reason with weil and an opinion with dass. Both send the verb to the end of the clause, and both need a comma before them. Ich mag Dokumentarfilme, weil man viel lernen kann. Ich finde, dass Krimis spannender als Komödien sind.
cards.lead: Film types are a good topic for opinions. Here you combine them with weil and dass, two small words that send the verb to the end, which you already know.

examples.de: Ich mag Dokumentarfilme, weil man viel lernen kann.
examples.en: I like documentaries because one can learn a lot.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass Horrorfilme zu gruselig sind.
examples.en: I think that horror films are too scary.

examples.de: Mira sieht gern Komödien, weil sie witzig sind.
examples.en: Mira likes comedies because they are funny.

deeper.text: You can use both in one sentence: Ich finde, dass Komödien lustiger als Krimis sind, weil man viel lacht. The second clause also sends its verb to the end. Do not start a new clause without a comma. And remember that in a dass clause the comparison and als come before the verb at the end.

example.de: Ich finde, dass Komödien lustiger als Krimis sind.
example.en: I think that comedies are funnier than crime films.

cards.more: Weil and dass work like a little door that sends the verb to the back of the room. After the door, you say who, what, when or where, and the verb comes last. Ich mag Dokumentarfilme is a main clause. Add weil and you get a second clause: weil man viel lernen kann. The verb that is conjugated, kann, is the last word. If there are two verbs, the infinitive lernen comes right before it.
steps: Say your main clause: Ich mag Dokumentarfilme
Put a comma and weil or dass
Add who or what and the details: man viel lernen
Put the conjugated verb last: kann.

cards.title: Plurals of film types
cards.body: When you speak about a type of film in general, use the plural without an article: Ich mag Krimis. Most types ending in -film add -e: Horrorfilme. Krimi adds -s, Komödie adds -n, and Genre adds -s. Learn the plural together with the noun.
cards.lead: You spoke about film types in the plural in the last cards without noticing. Here you look at how the plurals work, so you can say what you like in general.

examples.de: Was für Filme magst du?
examples.en: What kinds of films do you like?

examples.de: Ich mag Krimis und Komödien.
examples.en: I like crime films and comedies.

examples.de: Wir sehen oft Dokumentarfilme.
examples.en: We often watch documentaries.

deeper.text: Natives like short forms. Krimi is short for Kriminalfilm, and it can also mean a crime novel, ein Krimi to read. Documentary films are often called die Doku, plural die Dokus. Both short words are completely normal in daily talk, in TV listings and on streaming sites. Other short words you will see are der Thriller (plural die Thriller) and der Western. They belong to the same group, so you can name any film type.

example.de: Mira sieht gern Dokus.
example.en: Mira likes watching documentaries.

cards.more: In general talk you use the plural with no article, like English: I like comedies, not I like the comedies. The plural endings are easy to see: all the words ending in -film just take an -e. Two words are different: Krimi gets an -s, Komödie an -n. Genre gets an -s, too. Write the plural next to every noun in your notebook. The question Was für Filme magst du? is a fixed piece; you can use it without thinking about every word.

lessons.title: Worum geht es? Plots and reading long texts
lessons.goal: Say what a film is about with handelt von and Es geht um, tell a plot in the present, name the people in a film, read long texts with a four-step plan and report what a text says.

grammar.topic: film plots and reading long texts
grammar.point: Der Film handelt von + dative says what a film is about (von einem Mann, von einer Frau, von zwei Freunden). Es geht um + accusative is a chunk: Worum geht es? Tell a plot in the present with Am Anfang, dann and am Ende. Read long texts with four steps: title and pictures, questions, key words, guess. Report a text with Der Text sagt, dass ... or Im Text steht, dass .... Drehen has the Perfekt hat gedreht.
grammar.oneLine: Der Film handelt von einem Mann. Am Anfang trifft er eine Frau, und am Ende gehen alle nach Hause.

mistake.wrong: Der Film handelt von ein Mann.
mistake.right: Der Film handelt von einem Mann.
mistake.why: Von always takes the dative. For a der or das noun the dative of ein is einem.

terms.meaning: the case after von; ein becomes einem (der, das words) or einer (die words)
the story of a film or book; in German you tell it in the present tense
an important word that carries the main idea of a text

cards.title: Before we start: what is it about?
cards.body: A friend asks you: Worum geht es in dem Film? To answer, you need two short patterns: Der Film handelt von ... and Es geht um .... Today you also learn how to read a long text without panic, because long texts about films are full of words that you do not know yet, and that is fine.

examples.de: Ich mag Krimis.
examples.en: I like crime films.
examples.why: You know this already: your opinion about a film type.

examples.de: Das Buch ist von Frau Weber.
examples.en: The book is by Frau Weber.
examples.why: You know this too: von with a person.

examples.de: Der Film handelt von einer Schauspielerin.
examples.en: The film is about an actress.
examples.why: New today: von + dative says what the film is about.

cards.more: Imagine that you tell a friend about a film in one sentence, like the back of a DVD box: This film is about a girl and her dog. You do not tell the whole story. In German you say Der Film handelt von einem Mädchen und einem Hund. After von you always use the dative, which you know from A1. Today you also get a plan for reading long texts: look first, ask questions, mark key words and guess.
steps: You already know: Ich mag Krimis. (lesson 7) and Das Buch ist von Frau Weber.
New today: Der Film handelt von einer Schauspielerin. and Es geht um ...
By the end you can: say what a film is about and read a long film text with a plan.

cards.title: What is it about? handelt von and es geht um
cards.body: Two ways to say what something is about. Der Film handelt von + dative: von einem Mann, von einer Frau, von zwei Freunden. Es geht um + accusative: um einen Mann. Learn Es geht um ... as a chunk, and ask: Worum geht es?
cards.lead: A friend asks what a film is about. Two short patterns answer that question, and you already know the cases that follow them: the dative after von and the accusative after um.

examples.de: Der Film handelt von einer Schauspielerin.
examples.en: The film is about an actress.

examples.de: Das Buch handelt von einem Hund.
examples.en: The book is about a dog.

examples.de: Es geht um einen Mann und eine Katze.
examples.en: It is about a man and a cat.

deeper.text: English says about for both patterns, but German keeps a small difference. Handeln von is for stories, films, books and texts: it says what the story deals with. Es geht um is for any topic, also for talks and problems: Worum geht es in dem Gespräch? Es geht um Geld. Es geht um is also what you say when something matters to you. Both patterns are fixed, so es and geht never change.

example.de: Worum geht es in dem Gespräch? – Es geht um Geld.
example.en: What is the conversation about? – It is about money.

cards.more: Two little bridges lead to the same place. With handelt von the film is the subject: Der Film handelt von einem Hund. With Es geht um the word es is the subject, and it never changes: Es geht um einen Hund. After von you use the dative, after um the accusative. If you are not sure which one, remember von einem, um einen. The question for both is Worum geht es? You will hear it a lot when people talk about films and books.

rows: Der Film handelt von einem Mann.
Das Buch handelt von einer Katze.
Die Serie handelt von zwei Freunden.

cards.title: People in a film
cards.body: A film needs people. The man is der Schauspieler, the woman die Schauspielerin: add -in for a woman. The same works for der Regisseur and die Regisseurin. The leading role is die Hauptrolle. The hero is der Held, the heroine is die Heldin.
cards.lead: Now you can say what a film is about. Next you name the people who make the film and the people in it, with the pattern for male and female forms.

examples.de: Die Schauspielerin spielt die Hauptrolle.
examples.en: The actress plays the leading role.

examples.de: Der Regisseur ist berühmt.
examples.en: The director is famous.

examples.de: Der Held ist ein Lehrer.
examples.en: The hero is a teacher.

deeper.text: For a mixed group the traditional plural is the male form: die Schauspieler can mean actors of all genders. Today many people write Schauspieler:innen or say Schauspielerinnen und Schauspieler to include everybody. You will see all three in the media. The -in rule works for many jobs, not only for film: der Lehrer, die Lehrerin; der Kollege, die Kollegin. Der Held follows the rule too: die Heldin.

example.de: Die Heldin ist stark.
example.en: The heroine is strong.

cards.more: German has a simple way to make female words for people: add -in. Lehrer becomes Lehrerin, Schauspieler becomes Schauspielerin, Regisseur becomes Regisseurin. In the plural you add -nen to the -in word: die Schauspielerinnen. The hero follows the same rule: der Held, die Heldin. For now you only need them as the subject of a sentence, for example Der Held ist stark. The leading role, die Hauptrolle, is the biggest part in the film.

cards.title: The plot in the present: Am Anfang, dann, am Ende
cards.body: To tell a film plot, use the present tense, even if the film is old. Order the story with three time words: Am Anfang (at the beginning), dann (then), am Ende (at the end). The verb stays in second place: Am Anfang trifft ein Mann eine Frau.
cards.lead: You can now say who is in a film. A plot also needs an order: first this, then that, and at the end this. Three small time words do this job, and the present tense tells the story.

examples.de: Am Anfang trifft ein Mann eine Frau.
examples.en: At the beginning a man meets a woman.

examples.de: Dann verliert die Frau das Handy.
examples.en: Then the woman loses the phone.

examples.de: Am Ende gehen alle zusammen nach Hause.
examples.en: At the end everyone goes home together.

deeper.text: Natives use more words than dann to move a story along. Zuerst means first, danach means after that and schließlich means finally. Like dann they stand in place 1, so the verb follows at once: Zuerst trifft ein Mann eine Frau. Danach verliert die Frau das Handy. Schließlich gehen alle nach Hause. A longer plot sounds better when you change the words instead of using dann three times.

example.de: Schließlich finden alle den Hund.
example.en: Finally everyone finds the dog.

cards.more: When you tell a plot you act like a film commentator who sees the film right now. That is why German uses the present tense: Am Anfang trifft ein Mann eine Frau. Use am Anfang to start, dann for the middle and am Ende for the end. These words come first, so the verb comes second and the subject after the verb. It is the rule you know from A1: the verb is always in second place in a statement.

rows: Am Anfang trifft ein Mann eine Frau.
Dann verliert die Frau das Handy.
Am Ende gehen alle nach Hause.

cards.title: Strategy: how to read a long text
cards.body: A long text is not a reason to panic. Use four steps. One: look at the title and the pictures. Two: ask questions, for example Worum geht es? Wer spielt? Wo? Three: mark the key words you know. Four: guess the words you do not know. You do not need to translate every word.
cards.lead: Film descriptions and comments can be long. Before you read word by word, a short plan helps you to find the main points fast and to stay calm when you meet new words.

examples.de: Worum geht es?
examples.en: What is it about?

examples.de: Wer spielt die Hauptrolle?
examples.en: Who plays the leading role?

examples.de: Wo spielt der Film?
examples.en: Where does the film take place?

deeper.text: The most important point is step four: you can understand a text although you do not know every word. Look at the words around the new word. For example in Der Held ist stark und hat keine Angst you may not know Angst, but you can guess that it has to do with feeling. If a word is not important for the main idea, skip it.

example.de: Wer ist der Held im Film?
example.en: Who is the hero of the film?

cards.more: Think of a detective who looks at a room. First the detective looks at the whole room (title and pictures). Then asks questions: who, what, where? Then looks for clues (key words). If there is a thing that the detective does not know, he does not give up: he looks at the other things around it and guesses. You do the same with a text. You do not have to understand everything to understand the main idea. Try this plan every time you meet a long text.
steps: Look at the title and the pictures: what kind of text is it?
Ask questions: Worum geht es? Wer? Wo?
Mark the key words that you know (names, numbers, film words).
Guess the words that you do not know from the words around them. Do not translate every word.

cards.title: What the text says: dass
cards.body: Use a dass clause to report what a text says: Der Text sagt, dass ... or Im Text steht, dass .... The verb of the dass clause goes to the end, as you know. Use it to answer questions about a text in German.
cards.lead: After you have read a text with your plan, you often have to say what it says. For this you use the dass clause again, with new opening words.

examples.de: Der Text sagt, dass der Film spannend ist.
examples.en: The text says that the film is exciting.

examples.de: Im Text steht, dass die Schauspielerin berühmt ist.
examples.en: The text says that the actress is famous.

examples.de: Im Text steht, dass der Film traurig ist.
examples.en: The text says that the film is sad.

deeper.text: Many verbs of reporting open a dass clause, not only sagen and stehen. Schreiben works well for texts, messages and comments: Anna schreibt, dass der Film super ist. Stehen is the special verb for printed words: Im Text steht, dass ... literally means in the text stands that. You use it for what is written in a text, a letter or on a sign, while sagen sounds like a person speaking.

example.de: Anna schreibt, dass der Film super ist.
example.en: Anna writes that the film is great.

cards.more: You already say Ich weiß, dass ... and Ich glaube, dass .... Now you replace the person with a text: Der Text sagt, dass ... The rule is exactly the same. Put a comma, add dass, say the details, and put the verb last. The expression Im Text steht, dass ... is very common when you talk about what you read. It literally says: in the text stands, that. Use it whenever you answer a question about a reading text.
steps: Say where the information is: Der Text sagt, / Im Text steht,
Add dass
Say what the text says: der Film spannend
Put the verb at the end: ist.

cards.title: Film facts in the Perfekt: drehen
cards.body: To shoot a film is drehen. It is a regular verb, and its Perfekt is hat gedreht: Die Schauspielerin hat in Berlin gedreht. Use it for facts about how a film was made. In a dass clause the helper verb goes last: ..., dass der Regisseur den Film gedreht hat.
cards.lead: You know the Perfekt with haben. Here you use it for the work behind a film, with the new verb drehen, so you can say where and by whom a film was shot.

examples.de: Die Schauspielerin hat in Berlin gedreht.
examples.en: The actress was filming in Berlin.

examples.de: Der Regisseur hat den Film in Hamburg gedreht.
examples.en: The director shot the film in Hamburg.

examples.de: Ich weiß, dass der Regisseur den Film gedreht hat.
examples.en: I know that the director has shot the film.

deeper.text: Drehen also means to turn, but in a film context it means to shoot. The Perfekt is regular: ge- + stem + -t, so gedreht. The helper verb is haben: ich habe gedreht, er hat gedreht. We have shot a video is Wir haben ein Video gedreht. The same pattern works for every regular verb that you know, for example gespielt.

example.de: Wir haben ein Video gedreht.
example.en: We shot a video.

cards.more: Perfekt means two parts: a helper (haben) in second place and the participle at the end. For drehen the participle is gedreht: ge-, the stem dreh, and -t. In a main clause it looks like a frame: Der Regisseur hat den Film in Hamburg gedreht. In a dass clause, the order changes at the end: gedreht hat. Say it a few times aloud. Facts about a film are often in the Perfekt: who has shot it, where, and when.

lessons.title: Kino! Kino! Writing a film comment
lessons.goal: Write a short film comment in five parts with the Perfekt, handelt von, a comparison with dass, a star rating and a recommendation, and plan a film evening with friends.

grammar.point: A film comment has five parts: what you saw and when (Perfekt), what it is about (handelt von + dative), your opinion (dass + comparison, verb last), a rating (fünf von fünf Sternen) and your advice (Ich empfehle ..., weil ...). Use man and the Perfekt with drehen for film locations, and the present tense with modals to plan a film evening.
grammar.oneLine: Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war, und ich empfehle den Film.

mistake.wrong: Ich finde, dass der Film war besser als das Buch.
mistake.right: Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war.
mistake.why: In a dass clause the conjugated verb goes to the end, after the comparison.

terms.meaning: a short text that you write online to say what you think about something
a mark for something, for example stars; fünf von fünf Sternen is the best
a place where a film is shot

cards.title: Before we start: tell others what you think
cards.body: After a good film you want to tell somebody. Online you write a short comment: what you saw, what it is about, what you think and whether others should see it. Today you put everything from this chapter together into one comment, and you add a few useful phrases like fünf von fünf Sternen.

examples.de: Der Film handelt von einer Schauspielerin.
examples.en: The film is about an actress.
examples.why: You know this already: what the film is about (lesson 8).

examples.de: Meiner Meinung nach ist das Buch besser als der Film.
examples.en: In my opinion the book is better than the film.
examples.why: You know this too: an opinion with a comparison.

examples.de: Gestern habe ich einen Film gesehen, und ich finde, dass er spannend war.
examples.en: Yesterday I saw a film and I think that it was exciting.
examples.why: New today: all the parts together in one comment.

cards.more: A comment is like a small postcard from the cinema. You say what you saw, you say what it is about, you tell your opinion and you give advice to the reader. You have all the tools already: the Perfekt for what you saw, handelt von for the story, comparisons and dass for your opinion, weil for the reason. Today you only learn the order of the parts, a few new words like Kinokarte and Leinwand, and how to give a rating.
steps: You already know: Der Film handelt von ... (lesson 8) and Meiner Meinung nach ... (chapter 2).
New today: the five parts of a film comment and a rating like fünf von fünf Sternen.
By the end you can: write a short comment about a film for other people.

cards.title: The parts of a film comment
cards.body: A good comment has five parts in this order. One: what did you see and when? Two: what is it about? Three: what do you think, with a comparison and dass? Four: your rating. Five: your advice. Each part is one sentence, so the comment has about five sentences.
cards.lead: You have many tools now. A plan with five parts puts them in order, so that other people can follow your comment and you do not forget anything.

examples.de: Gestern habe ich einen Film gesehen.
examples.en: Yesterday I saw a film.

examples.de: Der Film handelt von einem Hund.
examples.en: The film is about a dog.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war.
examples.en: I think that the film was better than the book.

deeper.text: Notice the verb in the opinion sentence: war, not ist. When you talk about a film you have already seen, natives use war and hatte, not the Perfekt of sein and haben. Ich finde, dass der Film toll war sounds natural; ist toll gewesen sounds odd. You already know this rule from the past-tense lesson in chapter 2. For all other verbs, use the Perfekt: gesehen, gedreht, gelacht.

example.de: Ich finde, dass der Film sehr witzig war.
example.en: I think that the film was very funny.

cards.more: Plan your comment like a short story with five little boxes. Box one is the setting: when and what you saw. Box two is the content: what is it about. Box three is your opinion: use dass and a comparison. Box four is the rating, and box five is the advice for the reader. You do not have to write long sentences. Short sentences are good and easy to read. Check the verb at the end of each clause with dass or weil.

Der Film handelt von einem Hund.
Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war.
Der Film hat vier von fünf Sternen.
Ich empfehle den Film, weil er witzig ist.

What is it about? Der Film handelt von einem Hund.
What do you think? Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war.
Your rating and advice: vier von fünf Sternen. Ich empfehle den Film.

cards.title: Rating a film: fünf von fünf Sternen
cards.body: Online people rate films with stars. Say it as a fixed chunk: fünf von fünf Sternen (five out of five stars). Use haben: Der Film hat vier von fünf Sternen. Learn the chunk as one piece, with Sternen at the end.
cards.lead: Comments online often end with stars. You learn the chunk as one piece, so you can rate a film without any new grammar.

examples.de: Der Film hat fünf von fünf Sternen.
examples.en: The film has five out of five stars.

examples.de: Die Serie hat drei von fünf Sternen.
examples.en: The series has three out of five stars.

examples.de: Der Film ist sehr gut, aber das Buch ist besser.
examples.en: The film is very good, but the book is better.

deeper.text: Stars have a singular, too. For one star say einen Stern: Der Film hat nur einen Stern. Natives also give the stars, like a teacher giving marks: Ich gebe dem Film fünf Sterne. Here the film is the person who receives and the stars are the thing that is given, exactly like Ben gibt mir das Buch. Keep the chunk fünf von fünf Sternen for the written rating, and use this sentence when you speak.

example.de: Ich gebe dem Film fünf Sterne.
example.en: I give the film five stars.

cards.more: A star rating is like a school grade, but from one to five stars, and more is better. In German you say how many stars out of five: fünf von fünf Sternen, vier von fünf Sternen, drei von fünf Sternen. You do not have to understand the ending -n in Sternen now; it is part of the chunk. Just say it as one piece. Then add a short reason with weil if you like: weil der Film so spannend ist.

rows: Der Film hat fünf von fünf Sternen.
Die Serie hat vier von fünf Sternen.
Das Buch hat drei von fünf Sternen.

cards.title: Cinema culture: ticket, screen, popcorn, premiere
cards.body: These words belong to a visit to the cinema. You buy a Kinokarte and you sit in front of the Leinwand. Many people eat Popcorn. A Premiere is the first showing of a film. In summer you can watch a film in the park, and there is a famous Filmfestival in Berlin.
cards.lead: Before you write about a film, you need the words around the cinema. Here are the most useful ones, with a little culture from German-speaking countries.

examples.de: Die Kinokarte kostet zehn Euro.
examples.en: The cinema ticket costs ten euros.

examples.de: Im Kino esse ich gern Popcorn.
examples.en: In the cinema I like to eat popcorn.

examples.de: Die Leinwand im Park ist sehr groß.
examples.en: The screen in the park is very big.

deeper.text: In Germany most foreign films are dubbed: the actors speak German, and the film is synchronisiert (dubbed). If you want the original voices, look for OmU in the programme. It means Original mit Untertiteln, the original language with subtitles. Many cinemas also have a cheaper day, often early in the week, called Kinotag. So before you buy a Kinokarte, check whether the film is synchronisiert or OmU. It changes how much you can learn.

example.de: Ich sehe den Film lieber im Original.
example.en: I prefer to watch the film in the original.

cards.more: Cinema words are a small family. The Kinokarte is your ticket, the Leinwand is the big white screen, Popcorn is the snack, and the Premiere is the first night. In German-speaking countries many people like to see films outside in summer, in a park or a garden. A Filmfestival is a big event where many films are shown, and the best-known one in Germany is in Berlin. For your own writing, use the simple phrase das Filmfestival in Berlin.

cards.title: Drehorte: where films are made
cards.body: A Drehort is a place where a film is shot. Many films have been shot in German-speaking cities, for example Berlin, Hamburg, München, Wien and Zürich. Use man and the Perfekt with drehen: In Berlin hat man viele Filme gedreht.
cards.lead: You know drehen in the Perfekt from lesson 8. Now you use it with places, so you can say where a film was shot and talk about film locations.

examples.de: Berlin ist ein Drehort für viele Filme.
examples.en: Berlin is a film location for many films.

examples.de: In Berlin hat man viele Filme gedreht.
examples.en: Many films have been shot in Berlin.

examples.de: Man hat auch in Wien und in Zürich gedreht.
examples.en: Films have also been shot in Vienna and Zurich.

deeper.text: The word Ort (place) builds many useful compound nouns, and all of them are der words, because Ort is der. Besides der Drehort you will meet der Wohnort, the place where you live, and der Geburtsort, the place where you were born. The plural of Ort is die Orte, so die Drehorte, die Wohnorte. The same trick as with Film in lesson 7: the last part gives the article.

example.de: Mein Wohnort ist Berlin.
example.en: My place of residence is Berlin.

cards.more: A Drehort is made of drehen (to shoot) and Ort (place). Cities are often the stars of a film: the streets, the park, the old houses. When you do not know who shot a film, say man: Man hat in Wien gedreht. When you do know, use the person: Der Regisseur hat in Berlin gedreht. Both are Perfekt with haben, and the participle gedreht is always at the end of the main clause. In a dass clause the helper verb hat comes last.

rows: In Berlin hat man viele Filme gedreht.
Man hat auch in Wien gedreht.
Man hat auch in Zürich gedreht.

cards.title: Picknick im Park: plan an evening together
cards.body: The flat share wants to watch a film in the park. To plan, ask a question first, then make a suggestion, then share the tasks. Habt ihr Zeit? Wir können ein Picknick machen. Ben bringt das Popcorn mit. Use the present tense and modal verbs, as you know them.
cards.lead: A comment is not the only way to talk about a film. Often you plan to see one together. You already know the phrases for a plan, so here you combine them in a small dialogue.

examples.de: Habt ihr am Samstag Zeit?
examples.en: Do you have time on Saturday?

examples.de: Wir können im Park ein Picknick machen.
examples.en: We can have a picnic in the park.

examples.de: Ben bringt das Popcorn mit, und Mira kauft die Kinokarten.
examples.en: Ben brings the popcorn and Mira buys the cinema tickets.

deeper.text: To suggest something, natives often use a question with sollen: Sollen wir ein Picknick machen? It is friendlier than a statement, because the other person decides. Sollen is a modal, so you already know the pattern: the second verb goes to the end. You can answer Ja, gern! or Na ja ... when you are not sure. Use it for plans like picnics, films and cinema evenings.

example.de: Sollen wir um acht Uhr im Park sein?
example.en: Shall we be in the park at eight o'clock?

cards.more: To plan something with friends, use short, friendly sentences. First a question: Habt ihr am Samstag Zeit? Then an idea with können: Wir können ein Picknick machen. Then the tasks: Ben bringt das Popcorn mit. Mira kauft die Kinokarten. With mitbringen the little word mit goes to the end of the main clause. Everything is in the present tense, even for the future, with a time word like am Samstag. Easy and natural.

cards.title: A model comment by Anna
cards.body: Here is a model comment by Anna with all five parts: Gestern habe ich einen Film gesehen. Er handelt von einem Hund. Ich finde, dass der Film besser als das Buch war. Er hat vier von fünf Sternen. Ich empfehle den Film, weil er sehr witzig ist.
cards.lead: You have the five parts. Now you read Anna's whole comment and check the verb in every dass or weil clause. Use this model for your own comment.

examples.de: Ich empfehle den Film, weil er sehr witzig ist.
examples.en: I recommend the film because it is very funny.

deeper.text: Use the checklist: Is there a comma before dass and weil? Is the conjugated verb the last word in the clause? Did you use als after the comparison? Did you say what the film is about with handelt von and the dative? Ich empfehle ... is a fixed opener: after empfehlen comes the accusative, den Film.

example.de: Ich empfehle den Film.
example.en: I recommend the film.

cards.more: Look at the model like a recipe. Each sentence is one ingredient: when you saw it, what it is about, what you think, the stars, the advice. Anna uses war in the dass clause, hat in the Perfekt and ist after weil. The verb is always in the right place. When you write your own comment, copy this order and change the words. Then read it again and look at the commas and the end of each clause.
